$description: Contrast contracts (PRD §10.3, TR-07). This file is the machine-readable form of AR-07 and AR-08: every pairing a component can actually render is declared here and verified at build time. It is deliberately explicit rather than inferred — an inferred check silently misses the pair nobody thought to declare, and 'we did not think of it' is precisely how contrast failures reach production.

large-text.note: Applies at >=24px regular or >=18.66px bold — font.size.large-text-threshold.

enhanced.note: Not required by the AA target. Applied only to the high-contrast theme, where the whole point is to exceed AA.

contracts.note: Placeholder is never the sole label (AR-11), but when shown it must be readable.
SC 1.4.3 exempts inactive controls. AAL meets the ratio anyway — see exemptions[] for why we decline the exemption.
Validation error text (AR-12). Colour is never the only signal — icon and text always accompany it (AR-13).
The boundary of a text input IS a UI component boundary under 1.4.11 — a field the user cannot locate is a field they cannot fill.

Selection state must be perceivable as a state change. The validator originally checked selected.bg here and FAILED it at 1.24:1 — correctly, because a tint that faint cannot convey state. The fix was to introduce an explicit indicator rather than to darken the tint into an unreadable wash. See exemptions[] for selected.bg.

focusRing.$description: AR-05 / SC 1.4.11. The two-tone ring (PRD §10.5) passes against a given background when AT LEAST ONE tone reaches 3:1 — that is the whole point of two tones: the pair survives light and dark surfaces without the library knowing what the consumer put behind the control.

exemptions.reason: Purely decorative dividers that convey no information and do not bound an interactive control. 1.4.11 applies to parts required to identify a component or its state; these are neither. Every INFORMATIVE boundary uses color.border.default, which is contract-checked.
exemptions.review: Re-confirm during the expert WCAG review (PRD §13.2) — if any component uses border.subtle to bound a control, this exemption is void and that component is the defect.

exemptions.reason: Modal backdrop. Decorative dimming only; inertness is conveyed by the `inert` attribute and focus trapping (AR-15), never by the scrim's appearance.

Decorative reinforcement of selection, not the indicator itself. The perceivable state change is carried by color.selected.border (contract 'selected-indicator', 3:1 enforced) plus aria-selected in the accessibility tree (AR-16). The tint stays subtle deliberately: raising it to 3:1 against the page would force selected.text down toward the 4.5:1 floor and make selected rows visually shout.
exemptions.review: VOID IF: any component conveys selection using selected.bg WITHOUT also rendering selected.border. Check every component that has a selected state — Listbox option, Tabs tab, Table row, Menu item — during the expert WCAG review (PRD §13.2). If one relies on the tint alone, that component is the defect and this exemption does not cover it.
exemptions.originally-failed: 1.24:1 (light), 1.20:1 (dark) — recorded so the audit trail shows this exemption came from a real failure that was designed out, not from a threshold that was lowered.

exemptions.reason: WCAG 1.4.3 exempts text in inactive user-interface components. AAL declines that exemption and holds disabled text to 4.5:1 anyway: a user who cannot read a disabled control cannot tell WHAT is unavailable, and the exemption exists for legacy reasons rather than user benefit. Recorded here so that exceeding the standard is visibly a decision.
